card: Parallelizes BIP 157/158 compact block filter evaluation during wallet fast rescans using a worker thread pool. Introduces the -walletpar configuration option to control wallet concurrency, defaulting to auto-detecting core count up to 8 threads. Fast wallet rescans currently evaluate block filters sequentially on a single core, leaving other cores idle when scanning long chain intervals. On mainnet benchmarks scanning 200,000 blocks, rescan duration dropped from 272 seconds to 34.8 seconds with 8 threads (an ~7.8x speedup). Block reading, matching, and keypool top-ups remain serialized on the main thread, while in-flight negative filter verdicts are re-checked against newly derived descriptor scripts.
changed_since_previous: Added periodic progress logging and disk persistence at interval boundaries during parallel block checks, and updated functional and unit tests to explicitly test both serial and parallel paths.
evidence: Author's mainnet benchmark using hyperfine across 200,000 blocks (heights 700,000 to 900,000): master completed in 272.2 seconds, 1 thread completed in 275.0 seconds, and 8 threads completed in 34.8 seconds (~7.8x speedup).
problem: Fast wallet rescans check compact block filters sequentially on a single thread. When rescanning large block ranges or restoring wallets on multi-core systems, available CPU cores sit idle and rescans take minutes.

risk.why: Flaws in filter evaluation, race conditions during keypool top-up script patching, or dropped blocks in the pipeline could cause wallets to miss incoming transactions and report incorrect balances.

scope_notes: Touches wallet scanning pipelines extensively, introducing thread pool scheduling and handling incremental script set updates concurrently with filter evaluations.
summary: Parallelizes BIP 157/158 compact block filter evaluation during wallet fast rescans using a bounded worker thread pool. Adds the -walletpar configuration option (defaulting to auto-detected CPU cores up to 8 threads) to control wallet concurrency. Block reading and wallet state modifications remain serialized on the main thread, while filter checks are batched across threads and keypool top-ups re-check in-flight negative verdicts against newly added descriptor scripts.
